# Synthetic Caphyon/MSI scope fixtures

These fixtures test emitted signer and anti-analysis findings across synthetic CFBF/OLE parents. The parent streams carry OLE SummaryInformation with an `Installation Database` title, a Google application claim (or a near miss), one-token subject, non-vendor author, an `AsAdmin` marker, and enough inert streams to exercise the current MSI/OLE selectors. The PE members are inert DLLs compiled only to expose the four imports required by `msi-embedded-anti-analysis-loader`.

The Authenticode certificate is synthetic, self-signed, and untrusted. Its subject organization is `Caphyon SRL` solely to exercise Cleave's normalized signer-name emission. The key was generated outside the repository and was not retained here. The CMS signature contains a synthetic claimed image digest; it proves only that Cleave emits the signer claim from the certificate table. It does not establish trusted provenance or that the signature authenticates the PE image. None of these PE files is executed.

The `.ole` parents are intentionally CFBF/OLE fixtures rather than installable Windows Installer databases. They avoid MSI stream-name classification so the outer specimen is analyzed as `OleDoc`, allowing the current `oledoc`-scoped rules to be exercised. The emitted MSI traits therefore test the current metadata selectors, not Windows Installer installability.

`cases.json` checks the ordinary analyzer's emitted findings for a signed loader in one child, signer and loader in separate children, a non-Google parent, and an unsigned loader. The first two specimens currently emit `google-branded-caphyon-embedded-msi`, including the separate-child control. This is an observed cross-child association; the case matrix records it so a later scope correction can turn it into a regression control.

The focused checks use `scripts/check-taxonomy-cases.py --skip-traces`. A separate `test-rules` trace currently reports `google-branded-caphyon-embedded-msi` as not matched because its `for: [oledoc]` filter drops the signer finding originating in a PE member, even though the ordinary report emits the composite on both the same-child and separate-child specimens. That report/trace difference is recorded as an unresolved engine behavior, not treated as evidence that the edge is correctly scoped.
